opportunities.title: CCC CMD: HAZWOPER Training
opportunities.description:
The California Conservation Corps (CCC) is a state agency that oversees a program for 18 to 25-year old's through hands-on work and training to support California's natural resources as well as respond to state declared emergencies such as oil spills, earthquakes, fire, etc. HAZWOPER training and certification are critical for CCC Corpsmembers to ensure they are ready to safely respond to these disasters and to help build their skills towards potential future career opportunities.  

The CCC is looking for a contractor to deliver an on-site, in-person OSHA Compliant trainings at sites broken down below. Class size is 30 maximum students, minimum enrollment of 25. Instruction must be engaging and taught through various learning modalities. 

Please note: It will be a total of 28 courses (14 per Fiscal Year). New due date for BIDS is 9/09/2026.

opportunities.title: C26935001 Tijuana Estuary Restroom Improvements
opportunities.description:
The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to perform plumbing modifications, accessibility improvements, and facility upgrades at the Tijuana River Estuary Restrooms in San Diego County, California.

The work includes relocation and modification of existing drain and vent piping, replacement of plumbing components, conversion of urinals to waterless units, and relocation of flush valves to improve maintenance access and safer working conditions. opportunities.title: RFQ FOR MEDICAL EQUIPMENT DEPLOYMENT & LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT SERVICES
opportunities.description:
UC Davis Health in Sacramento, California requests Statements of Qualifications on or before 4 p.m. Monday, September 14, 2026, from qualified firms interested in providing Medical Equipment Deployment and Logistics Management services to support the Facilities Planning and Development department.

The University is seeking one (1) qualified Medical Equipment Deployment and Logistics firm to support typical construction and non-construction projects, including equipment replacement initiatives and relocations throughout the health system through a single point of contact. These efforts may involve UC Davis Health buildings and departments for inpatient, outpatient, and administrative (primarily office) spaces supporting the health system on the Sacramento campus and off-site locations. The firm selected will be expected to sign a Professional Services Agreement with a duration of 48 months and a dollar threshold not to exceed $1.5 million. 

The RFQ package with additional information and attachments can be downloaded directly from our website at https://health.ucdavis.edu/facilities/work-with-us/consultants/rfq starting Thursday, August 27, 2026. Statements of qualifications shall be specifically tailored to this RFQ, responding directly to the screening criteria (See RFQ document and Consultant Qualification form available on the above link). After Qualification Statements are received, a Screening Committee will review, conduct reference checks and recommend a short list of firms for interviews. A Selection Committee will conduct the discussions prior to selecting the successful firm.

The following is a list and brief description of several projects that are taking place within the UC Davis Health system and may require equipment support services:

#

	Project Name

	Description

	Est. Project Budget

1	DT Central Pharmacy Remodel	Remodel of the Davis Tower Basement Pharmacy.
	$10M>
2	ACC Rad Mammography	Replacing existing Mammo with GE and Siemens
	$10M>
3	Davis Tower Radiology 1835H & 1835I Upgrades	Remodel/upgrade of Radiology suites and equipment	$10M>
4	DT 1ST FLR RAD Nuclear Medicine Remodel	Remodel and deployment of GE equipment	$10M>
5	SESP OR Integration	Remodel and Steris integration upgrade of SESP ORs 
	$10M>
6	Cancer Center Progenitor Lab Expansion	Expansion/upgrade of existing Progenitor Lab facility  	$10M<
7	SESP 1P742 1P1745 RAD Replace CT Scanners	Remodel and replacement of CT scanners in SESP 	$10M<
8	X-Ray PCN Replacements	Remodel and replacement of Philips X-ray units in various ambulatory clinics in our patient care network	TBD
9	Annual Equipment Replacement	Direct equipment replacements of EOS/EOL for various hospital and clinical departments	TBD
10	ACC Clinic Relocations	Various clinical department relocations 
	TBD
		
Additional projects will be initiated during this agreement, and the firm must demonstrate the ability to adapt to growing and shrinking project demands.

The selected firm will be responsible for the end-to-end deployment, logistics and activation of equipment scope for the hospital's capital construction and renovation projects, including equipment replacement and relocation initiatives. Reporting to the Medical Equipment Program Manager within the FP&D department, this role leads equipment deployment planning, manages and oversees fulfillment logistics in partnership with all stakeholders and serves as the central logistical coordination point for all stakeholders, including UC Davis Health support service departments, such as but not limited to Clinical Engineering, Plant Operations & Maintenance, Distribution, Environmental Services, IT/IS, Security, Infection Prevention, Pharmacy Security. Equipment types are mobile assets, fixed assets, wall fixtures and other for all modalities. This support is critical to ensure equipment is verified as received, transferred, staged, and is installed on schedule and in a manner that safeguards continuous hospital operations and patient safety.

Your firm¿s statement of qualifications must be received no later than 4 p.m. September 14, 2026, via upload link provided by Leila Couceiro, Contracts Manager. Applicants should request an upload link to Leila (lccouceiro@health.ucdavis.edu) no later than Friday, September 11, 2026.

Every effort will be made to ensure that all persons have equal access to contracts and other business opportunities with the University within the limits imposed by law or University policy. Each firm may be required to show evidence of its equal employment opportunity policy. The successful firm and their subconsultants will be required to follow the nondiscrimination requirements set forth in the Agreement documents and to pay prevailing wages at the location of the work. The work described in the Agreement is a public work subject to section 1771 of the California Labor Code.

Consultant/Design Professional shall pay all persons providing services and/or any labor on site, including any University location, no less than UC Fair Wage and shall comply with all applicable federal, state and local working condition requirements.

THE REGENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA                                             	        AUGUST 2026

opportunities.title: IFB# C26554001 Heavy Equipment Rental - Oceano Dunes District
opportunities.description:
The Oceano Dunes District (ODD) of CA State Parks, located in San Luis Obispo County, invites qualified firm to submit bid proposals for heavy equipment rental services (tractor and scraper) for use in dust mitigation efforts within the district¿s sand dune and coastal environment for a duration of approximately four (4) months. 

Anticipated service period: October 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027.

The firm will provide equipment as described in Exhibit A, Attachment I- Scope of Work Detail (Photo examples of specified equipment in in Exhibit A, Attachment III -Sample Photos and Descriptions), within the attached Bid Package.

EQUIPMENT OVERVIEW
1.ONE (1) FULL SIZE RUBBER WIDE-TRACK TRACTOR, meeting the following specifications: 
	- Tracks may either be an independent quad-track or two (2) single contiguous tracks.
	- Tractor base weight shall be approximately 50,000 to 60,000-pounds; engine shall be rated at 500 to 600 horsepower.
	- Tractor shall include a 3-point hitch and drawbar to match scraper, see Section 2(c).
	- Tractor shall include enclosed cab, air conditioning, heating, air ride seat, functional gauges, switches and controls, full hydraulic cab controls for operating the scraper while in motion.

2.ONE (1) DUMP SCRAPER
	- Direct mount, pull behind, non-agriculture, non-ejector, dump scraper with hydraulic controls for lifting, scraping, loading and dumping capabilities while in motion.
	- Scraper must be compatible with the tractor requested in Section 2.b.
	- The scraper cutting width must match the tractor tread width, plus or minus 6 inches. (E.g. should the tractor create a 12-foot-wide track the scraper cutting width shall be 11.5 to 12.5 feet wide. The Ashland 2012CS and IMC 225CS are examples of desirable designs for these conditions.)

Bids should include fees associated with the delivery and pickup of equipment at ODD¿s Maintenance Yard: 900 Pacific Blvd., Oceano, CA 93445. 

Additional rental requirements and terms are included in the Bid Package.

Complete bids proposals must include all completed forms listed in on the Bidder¿s Checklist, including the checklist, within the Bid Package. 

Bids must respond to each item listed on the Cost Breakdown; partial bids will not be considered.

STATE OF CALIFORNIA                                                                                                                             DEPARTMENT OF GENERAL SERVICES                                                                                                        REAL ESTATE SERVICES DIVISION                                                                                                                       PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT BRANCH
ADVERTISEMENT FOR BIDS                        
JOB ORDER CONTRACT (JOC)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Central Region of California                                                                                                                          Contract No. TBD 

DIGITAL BIDS: The Project Management and Development Branch will receive Bids no later than 11:59 P.M. on Wednesday, September 16, 2026. See Project Manual Book 1 Invitation for Bids 00 11 00 for instructions regarding bid submissions.                                                                                                                                                                
SCOPE OF WORK: The Work includes a collection of tasks and related specifications that have pre-established Unit Prices. A JOC shall be used for the accomplishment of repair, alteration, construction, maintenance, rehabilitation, demolition, and construction of infrastructure and buildings by means of individual Job Orders issued under the JOC.   
DGS intends to award multiple Job Order Contracts, a fixed period, fixed unit price, and indefinite quantity contract under this single solicitation as determined by the lowest Combined Adjustment Factor. The DGS JOC program is established in accordance with California PCC §10113 et seq. 
The intent and purpose of this solicitation is to establish a JOC with a twenty-four (24) month initial contract term with the Work to be carried out in the Central Region of California Areas 1 and 2 (See Bid Form 00 41 00 for JOC Region Map).                                                                    
CSLB LICENSE REQUIRED TO BID: B

HEALTH AND SAFETY PROVISIONS: Contractor and all subcontractors shall abide by all health and safety mandates issued by federal, state, and local governments and/or public health officers as well as those issued by DGS, and worksite specific mandates. If multiple mandates exist, the Contractor and subcontractors shall abide by the most restrictive mandate. The term employee, worker, state worker or state employee in health and safety mandates includes contractor and subcontractor personnel. Costs associated with adhering to health and safety mandates are the responsibility of the Contractor.  Contractor is responsible for the tracking and compliance of health and safety mandates and may be audited upon request. 
The successful bidder shall furnish payment and performance surety bonds in the form prescribed by the State. Each initial bond shall be in the amount of $5,000,000 and executed by an admitted surety insurer licensed in the State of California and listed in the latest published United States Treasury Department list of Companies Holding Certificates of Authority as Acceptable Sureties on Federal Bonds and as Acceptable Reinsuring Companies. As Job Orders are awarded, and at the State's discretion, new surety bonds will be required in the amount of $2,500,000. At no time shall the aggregate amount of active Job Orders exceed the bonds.

opportunities.description:
ADVERTISEMENT FOR MATERIALS TESTING AND INSPECTION SERVICES

UCLA Health requests a written response to this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to select consultants to provide materials testing and deputy inspection services for various non-specific UCLA Health projects.  These services are anticipated to be available for renovations and remodels, infrastructure upgrades, seismic improvements, and utility and site developments for a specific list of projects that has yet to be determined.  

The University may select up to two consultants to provide services for non-project-specific assignments.  Each consultant selected will perform work under a Professional Services Agreement (PSA) with the University, with authorizations for specific assignments from UCLA Health as necessary over the term of the agreement, which may be up to 3 years, with an option to extend for up to an additional 3-year term.

The scope of services may vary based on the detailed requirements of each assigned task, with appropriate fees negotiated in accordance with UCLA policy at the time of each authorization. The anticipated aggregate fees range from $100,000 to $4,000,000 over the term of the PSA, with an option to extend the fee limit by an additional $2,000,000 should the contract duration be extended.  The selection of firms for services under this agreement does not guarantee the number of tasks assigned or the value of fees expended.

The selected consultant(s) will demonstrate familiarity with a full range of project types undertaken by UCLA Health (including new construction, renovations and remodels, infrastructure upgrades, seismic improvements, utility and site developments, and many other project types), and previous experience in public university settings is preferred but not required.

The complete RFQ packet will be available at
http://www.capitalprograms.ucla.edu/Contracts/RFQProjects on Friday, August 28, 2026.  Responses to the RFQ are due by or before 10:00 a.m. on Friday, September 18, 2026.   To download the complete RFQ packet, you must create a login and password.  Registration instructions are available at https://www.uclaplanroom.com/help/account.register.  Once in the UCLA Planroom, click the "RFQ" tab and search for the project to download.  Within the project "RFQ Document" tab, download (1) RFQ, (2) the Planroom RFQ-Upload Instructions, and (3) Appendix C and D Instructions. Failure to comply could result in your submission being overlooked.
  
Every effort will be made to ensure that all persons have equal access to contracts and other business opportunities with the University within limits imposed by law or University policy.  Each Candidate Firm may be required to show evidence of its equal employment opportunity policy.

opportunities.title: Salton Sea West Flood Resilience Study.
opportunities.description:
The study is located along the west side of the Salton Sea on routes 78 and 86 in Imperial County
and extends 10 miles into Riverside to address priority issues in the vicinity of Torres Martinez
Desert Cahuilla Indians. Study area roadway segments are experiencing an increasing number of
recurring washouts and flooding events due to larger/more frequent precipitation events (expected to increase 8.2% by 2085) and may cost the state millions. In the last ten years District 11 has spent
nearly $5 million on nine (9) separate washout/flooding Director¿s Orders (DO) emergency projects in the study area, reaffirming the need for a long-term solution to proactively address these climate impacts while ensuring that unnecessary expenditures are limited. This increasing number of events may lead to damaged infrastructure, road closures, delays, and potentially dangerous roadway conditions for the surrounding tribal lands and disadvantaged communities. Additionally, these
impacts combined may reduce access to key community amenities in surrounding cities and tribal
lands such as employment centers, healthcare, and schools.

opportunities.description:
You are invited to review and respond to this Invitation for Bid (IFB) entitled 26-117 ¿ Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) and Power Conditioning and Distribution Systems Maintenance Services at DMV Headquarters Building East and the DMV Central Utility Plant (CUP).

Purpose and Description of Services:  Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) and Power Conditioning and Distribution Systems Maintenance Services at DMV Headquarters Building East and the DMV Central Utility Plant (CUP).  

Term: Twenty-four (24) months (see Schedule of Events for proposed start date of contract).  See Exhibit A, Scope of Work, for a complete description of services.  

Total Estimated Contract Cost:  $104,734.42

Bidder Qualifications: 

A.	On March 4, 2022, Governor Gavin Newsom issued Executive Order N-6-22 regarding Economic Sanctions against Russia and Russian entities and individuals.  ¿Economic Sanctions¿ refers to sanctions imposed by the U.S. government in response to Russia¿s actions in Ukraine, as well as any sanctions imposed under state law.  By submitting a bid, the bidder represents that it is not a target of Economic Sanctions.  Should the State determine, at any time prior to the execution of a contract, that the bidder is a target of Economic Sanctions or is conducting prohibited transactions with sanctioned individuals or entities, that shall be grounds for rejection of the bidder¿s bid by the DMV.

B. Documentation substantiating this must be included with bid documents.

The bidder must demonstrate a sufficient depth of personnel such that multiple service events occurring at the same time will not cause a delay in service response to DMV.  The bidder must supply a list of qualified field service personnel within the four (4) hour response service area, list years of experience servicing Liebert Series 610 and Eaton Powerware 9355 Model 30 UPS equipment and provide base location of field service engineer. opportunities.title: RFI No. 26-001 Compensation and Restitution System Modernization
opportunities.description:
The California Victims Compensation Board (CalVCB) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to solicit innovative input from qualified vendors (Respondents) for a modernization solution to replace CalVCB's current claims processing system. 

The Compensation and Restitution System (CaRes) provides a means to capture and process all the information associated with a claim to determine eligibility. Bills are also captured and processed for benefit determination and then payments are processed and sent to the claimants and/or providers. 

CaRes is currently a workflow-based system that follows the claim through its life cycle. Work flows within the current system through work items generated and presented in queues for staff, with designated permissions. Reports are generated to review aging, assigned and processed work. The application comes in (online, via mail or email), and if accompanied by appropriate supporting information, an eligibility determination is made. If supporting information is absent, the application must be held and the supporting information requested - either from the claimant or external sources (i.e., crime reporting agencies, Department of Justice, etc.). Once a determination can be made, the application is either approved or denied, and any associated bills can be reviewed for processing. There is an emergency award process that allows for expedited reviews in dire circumstances. Both documentation of the emergency request and independent processing of the application must be available.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority (Authority) has issued Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for Collaborative Design-Build Services for Merced to Madera (M2M) Civil Works. The purpose of this procurement is to enter into a collaborative design-build agreement to complete the design and construction of civil works for the M2M project segment, which consists of approximately 30.3 miles of new high-speed rail guideway extending from just south of Mission Avenue in the City of Merced to the southern project interface at Construction Package 1 in Madera County. There are options for an extension to Downtown Merced and State Route 152 improvements.

Updates, including responses to written questions, and any additional addenda will be provided here on Cal eProcure.

RFQ Timeline for this procurement is as follows:
July 9, 2026: RFQ released on the California State Contracts Register (Cal eProcure) 
July 16, 2026: Pre-Bid Conference (East End Complex 
1500 Capitol Ave, Sacramento, CA 95814)

The California High-Speed Rail Authority (Authority) anticipates requesting approval to release a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for Collaborative Design-Build Services for the Merced to Madera Civil Works Project from its Board of Directors at its June 24, 2026 meeting.  

RFQ Timeline  

Subject to approval and direction by the Board of Directors, the anticipated timeline for the RFQ is as follows: 

June 24, 2026: Board of Directors consider approving release of RFQ  

July 2026: RFQ released on the California State Contracts Register (Cal eProcure)

A draft RFQ is available as an attachment to this event on Cal eProcure. Be advised that the collaborative design-build contract resulting from this procurement will require compliance with the Authority's Small Business Program.

opportunities.title: RFP# C26554003 - Avian Predator Services (Oceano Dunes District-State Parks)
opportunities.description:
The Oceano Dunes District, State Parks located in San Luis Obispo County requests proposals from qualified firms to provide avian predator specialist services to trap and relocate problem avian predators for the management of Western Snowy Plover (WSP) and California Least Tern (CLT) at Oceana Dunes State Vehicular Recreation Area (ODSVRA). All work will support the ongoing management of WSP and CLT at ODSVRA during the 2027, 2028, and 2029 breeding seasons (approximately, March 20 to September 10).

PROJECT SCOPE OVERVIEW

(Please reference the RFP package for detailed purpose and description of services)
Contractor will monitor avian predator activity, evaluate the threat of avian predators to nesting WSP and CLT, and determine which individual avian predators pose an unacceptable threat to the nesting success of WSP and CLT at ODSVRA. For all species deemed a threat to breeding WSP and CLT, contractor shall live trap, band, and relocate a sufficient distance away to lessen the chance they will return to the site. It is the contractor(s) responsibility to furnish all required tools, lure animals, traps, materials, smart phone and applications, labor, incidentals, and transportation to the nesting area.

The primary nesting area at ODSVRA is approximately 400 acres, however the contractor will be responsible for monitoring predator activity and trapping in the approximately 5,000 acres managed by the State. In addition, and on a limited basis, the contractor may need to track avian problem predators and their nesting locations when trapping is not possible on-site. Work off-site may involve surveillance, tracking and trapping of problem predators in the immediate vicinity of ODSVRA as needed for project success.
The contractor should expect to spend at least 30 hours per week monitoring avian predators at the site, including gulls within the nesting habitat.

Contractor will work closely with ODSVRA staff, the United States Department of Agriculture Wildlife Services (USDA) contractors, and other ODSVRA contractors, including, coordinating and communicating all work activities, attend meetings regularly, at least once per month, assist with training of avian predator identification and biology, and prepare daily field notes and a year-end summary report.


KEY ACTION DATES

RFP Release: September 4, 2026, at 2:00pm
Question Submittal Deadline: Monday, September 21, 2026, at 2:00pm
Answers to Questions posted to RFP event: Wednesday, September 23, 2026
Proposal Submission Deadline: Monday, September 30, 2026 at 2:00pm
Proposal Intent to Award Notice: Monday, October 7, 2026
Proposal Award: Monday, October 14, 2026 
(Please note, no public opening of bids will occur. RFP ¿ secondary solicitations do not require public opening. 


REQUIRED MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR PROPOSERS/FIRMS OVERVIEW
(Please reference the RFP package for details related to minimum qualifications )

1. Personnel assigned to this project must furnish the following permits or demonstrate progress towards obtaining them before March 1, 2027:
     - USFWS (Migratory Bird Treaty Office) federal depredation permit.
     - California state Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for relocation of species that are depredating other threatened and endangered species, and scientific collecting permit for each person on the project that refers to the MOU.
     - United States Geological Survey (USGS) Bird Banding Laboratory federal marking and banding permit for relocated species.

2. Three (3) years of independent experience monitoring, identifying, trapping, banding, and relocating raptors and other avian predators for the purpose of managing a threatened or endangered species, and specific experience working with the following: northern harrier, peregrine falcon, loggerhead shrike, American kestrel, merlin, great horned owl, barn owl, gull species, corvid species such as raven and crow, red-tailed hawk, Cooper¿s hawk, and sharp-shinned hawk.

3. One (1) year of independent predator management experience for the purpose of protecting the WSP and CLT.

4. Three (3) years¿ experience preparing detailed biological reports.

5. Experience and proficiency in use and techniques of the following trapping devices: bal-chatri, noose jackets, mist nets, dho-gazza, bownets, Swedish goshawk, and noose carpets.

6. Access to transportation to nesting sites, 4x4 vehicle is highly advised.

7. Ability to be reached in an emergency within 1 hour and respond onsite within 24 hours of notice.

8. Experience working in teams, with governmental entities, and predator removal permit requirements. 

9. Supply the Names, titles, addresses, and contact phone numbers for a minimum of three (3) firms that can attest to the skills and abilities of the proposing entity to conduct the work identified in this RFP. At least two (2) References will be contacted, and their responses will be considered in determining if firms and individuals meet the Minimum Qualifications in this RFP.


PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS OVERVIEW
(Please reference the RFP package for details related proposal requirements )

1. Work Plan and Schedule
Must include: 
     - Developed work plan and schedule, which identifies each task and/or milestones to be accomplished to reach project objectives. 
     - Discussion of activities to be conducted to achieve project objectives, including: 
     - Methods to ensure personnel availability and timely response to emergencies, 
     - Methods to ensure personnel access to necessary equipment and transportation,
     - Description of work plan and ability of contractor to be available for tracking predator activity, assisting in the lethal removal of predators, night surveys, and other tasks described in Purpose and Description of Services section of this RFP.  
     - Description of staff levels, schedules, and primary responsibilities of on-site staff.

2. Project Personnel Details
Must include: 
     - Documentation supporting experience of project personnel
     - Proposers background, references, and in-house capacities.

3. Cost Detail 
Cost proposal must include the total cost of the project over project period, with a detailed breakdown showing how the costs were determined.


PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS OVERVIEW
(Complete instructions are included in RFP Package)

Proposals must be complete and accurate and should provide straightforward and concise descriptions of the proposer's ability to satisfy the requirements of this RFP. 

All proposals must be submitted electronically via email as an attachment in Portable Document Format (PDF) to od.billing@parks.ca.gov by dates and times shown in Proposal Requirements and Information and the Key Action Dates. Proposals received after this date and time will not be considered.

All proposals must include the documents identi¿ed in the Proposal Documents. Proposals not including the proper ¿required attachments" shall be deemed non- responsive. A non-responsive proposal is one that does not meet the basic proposal requirements. The bidder¿s checklist includes a list of documents for submission.
 
Note: The Disabled Veteran business Enterprise (DVBE) participation requirement is waived for this solicitation. However, the Small Business (SB) and DVBE incentive still applies. Details are included in the RFP package. 


PROPOSAL EVALUATIONS

Award, if made, will be to the highest scored responsible proposal. The proposals that meet the minimum quali¿cations will be evaluated and scored according to criteria listed on the evaluation and reference forms (located within the RFP package) .

A minimum of (70) points must be achieved in this phase to be considered responsive, out of (100). Up to (40) points awarded for proposal quality and workplan; Up to (30) points awarded for experience and technical merit, and up to (30) points for total cost.

Additional details and sample evaluation tools that will be used for scoring proposals and references, are included in the RFQ package.


RFQ QUESTIONS

Questions regarding the RFQ should be emailed to OD.Billing@parks.ca.gov, by September 21, 2026. Answers to questions received will be posted publicly to this event posting by September 23, 2026.0

CONSULTING SERVICES

A Selection Committee will conduct the discussions prior to selecting the successful firm.

UC Davis Health is seeking consulting services to support environmental planning functions for individual projects or plans at the UC Davis Sacramento Campus and for off-site locations within the greater Sacramento Region for projects described in the RFQ. Services include performing environmental planning and environmental review for campus development projects, preparing CEQA and NEPA environmental documents, mitigation monitoring, and providing regulatory, editorial and strategic environmental planning support.

Up to 2 firms will be selected for these services. 

In responding to this RFQ, you must notify the University by Tuesday, September 29, 2026, to be provided a link to upload their Qualifications package. Questions and requests for the link to upload statements may be addressed via email only to Cori Costanza, Contracts Administrator at cruggiero@health.ucdavis.edu. opportunities.title: Prequalification of Prospective Bidders for Parking Lot E8 Repairs
opportunities.description:
NOTICE TO CONTRACTORS
Parking Lot E8 Repairs, Project Number PE825PK023
California State University, Long Beach
1250 Bellflower Blvd
Long Beach, CA 90840

The Trustees of the California State University will receive sealed bid proposals at the Design and
Construction Services Office located at 1331 Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach CA 90840, for furnishing
all labor and materials for construction of the above-named Project, Project Number PE825PK023,
for the California State University Long Beach campus. Proposals will be received in the abovementioned
office until 2:00 p.m. on November 12, 2026, in accordance with the contract documents,
at which time the proposals will be publicly opened and read.
The project shall be in accordance with the plans and specifications prepared by 19six Architects; 802
East Cota Street, Suite A, Santa Barbara; Ewa Pocwiardowska; (805) 963-1955 e-mail:
ewa@19six.com. The Owner¿s construction estimate is $3,700,000.

Scope:
In general, the work consists of the complete removal of the existing 4 inch asphalt pavement and the
upper 18 inches of soil (which includes 12-14 inches of cement-treated soil). The new asphalt section
will consist of a minimum of 4 inches of asphalt placed over non-expansive fill compacted to a
minimum of 95% relative compaction. The scope also includes converting 9 EV ready stalls to full
EV charging capability and restriping.

A pre-bid conference via Zoom has been scheduled for September 21, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Interested
bidders are strongly encouraged to attend via the following link: https://csulb.zoom.us/j/83022756577.
A mandatory pre-bid site walk has been scheduled for October 20, 2026. Interested bidders should
assemble at Parking Lot E8 on the South end of campus, along 7th Street.
Each bidder offering a proposal must comply with Bidding provisions of Article 2.00 et seq. in the
Contract General Conditions regarding the necessity to prequalify.

To apply, Bidders shall go to the following ¿PlanetBids¿ website, register, log in, and select the
Prequalification tab.
¿California State University, Office of the Chancellor, Vendor Portal¿
(https://www.planetbids.com/portal/portal.cfm?CompanyID=15331)

Questions regarding prequalification with the Chancellor¿s Office should be directed to the Trustees¿
Prequalification Administrator at cocm.prequal@calstate.edu. All required prequalification
documents must be submitted to the Chancellor¿s office by October 5, 2026.

In addition to being prequalified with the Chancellor¿s Office, all bidders must be prequalified with
California State University, Long Beach. This requires submitting responses to the Technical
Prequalification Questionnaire, which can be obtained on Planetbids. Questions and responses
should be directed to tammy.dinh@csulb.edu. The Technical Prequalification Questionnaire will be
reviewed at the campus level by California State University, Long Beach. All required prequalification documents must be submitted to California State University, Long Beach by October 5, 2026.

Prequalified contractors will be notifed by October 19, 2026 and will receive a bid proposal package.
All bidders must have attended the mandatory site walk, be prequalified with the Chancellor¿s
Office, and technically prequalified by California State University, Long Beach. All items in
the bid package must be completed and submitted for bids to qualify.

The Trustees require the successful bidder to achieve three percent (3%) DVBE participation in
contracting construction projects as established in the bidding documents, and bidders shall identify
the DVBEs to be used to satisfy this requirement in their bids.

DVBE Incentive: Additionally, the Trustees are granting a bid incentive for evaluation purposes only
to bidders that exceed the three (3) percent DVBE participation requirement. The level of DVBE incentive
will correlate to the level of participation; that is, the more DVBE participation proposed, the higher the
incentive. The bid incentives are as follows:
DVBE
Participation
Incentive
3.00% to 3.99% None
4.00% to 4.99% 1%
5.00% to 5.99% 2%
6.00% or more 3%

The DVBE incentive may not exceed $50,000 when used in combination with the Small Business
Preference; the cumulative adjustment amount shall not exceed $100,000. If the lowest responsive,
responsible bid is a California certified small business, the only bidders eligible for the incentive will
be California certified small businesses. Bidders shall contact the Trustees¿ DVBE Coordinator, Lily
Mikuni, at lily.mikuni@csulb.edu or via phone at (562)-985-5797.

Each bidder shall be familiar with all the provisions of the Contract General Conditions and
Supplementary General Conditions, especially the Insurance Requirements for the CSU Builders Risk
Insurance Program (BRIP) and for the CSU Owner-Controlled Insurance Program (OCIP). This
project will be enrolled into the BRIP, and may be enrolled into the OCIP, if so specified in the
Supplementary General Conditions. If OCIP is applicable to this project, Bidders may review OCIP
documents online at www.calstate.edu/ConstructionInsurancePrograms.

This project is a public works project and is subject to prevailing wage rate laws (Contract General

shall register to bid and work on public works projects with the Dept. of Industrial Relations, and
maintain current this registration pursuant to Labor Code section 1725.5. For more information, go to

opportunities.title: ASI Wellness Initiative, Project No: FL-2673
opportunities.description:
The Project approximately consists of the renovation and expansion of the existing CSUF Titan Student Union and Student Recreation Center to support the Associated Students Inc. (ASI) student wellness initiative and address evolving student needs. The existing Titan Student Union was originally constructed in 1976 and subsequently renovated and expanded in 1992 and 2016. The building currently comprises approximately 166,841 gross square feet. The project will renovate approximately 48,000 square feet of the existing facility and add an approximately 18,900 square foot, two-story addition on the south side of the building. Approximately 13,400 square feet of the new addition will be dedicated to Basic Needs programs and services.
The Student Recreation Center was constructed in 2008 and currently comprises 98,000 gross square feet. The project will renovate approximately 92,000 square feet of the existing facility and provide approximately 25,000 square feet of new construction. The proposed expansion includes a three-story addition on the south side of the building and a two-story addition on the west side to accommodate a new Wellness Center and expanded fitness areas. Approximately 3,100 square feet of the expansion is identified as deck space.
Together, the renovated and expanded facilities will provide a comprehensive range of student-focused programs and amenities, including campus dining and kitchen facilities; meeting spaces; offices; lounge and collaboration spaces; games and recreation spaces; Basic Needs services, including a food pantry, hygiene product dispensary, and Tuffy¿s Career Closet; fitness facilities; and a Wellness Center. The project will also include shared amenity areas, building support spaces, and other maintenance- and service-oriented spaces.
In addition to the building improvements, the project includes approximately 44,000 square feet of site improvements, including enhancements to the intramural field and associated sitework.

opportunities.title: HSR26-20 Cal CLEAN Partnership Agreement
opportunities.description:
** UPDATE (8/5/26): The SOQ due date has been changed to November 6, 2026. A revised schedule will be provided in a subsequent addendum.

** UPDATE (7/30/26): RFQ Addendum 1 for the Cal CLEAN Partnership has been released. Questions are due to the Authority by August 3, 2026. Please email CalCLEAN@hsr.ca.gov. 

** UPDATE (7/29/2026): Round 1 Questions and Responses have been posted. The Authority anticipates issuing Addendum 1 for the Cal CLEAN Partnership on 07/30/2026.

** UPDATE (7/20/26): Questions due to the Authority for Cal CLEAN Partnership Agreement is July 22, 2026. Please email CalCLEAN@hsr.ca.gov

** UPDATE (7/14/26): The Virtual Pre-Bid Conference for the Request for Qualifications for Cal CLEAN Partnership Agreement has been moved to Monday, July 20th, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. PST. Please see the updated Registration link.


The Authority is responsible for planning, designing, building, and operating the first high-speed rail system in the nation. California high-speed rail will connect the mega-regions of the state, contribute to economic development and a cleaner environment, create jobs, and preserve agricultural and protected lands. To pursue this goal, the California High-Speed Rail Authority has issued a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for a private-sector development partner (Developer) to enter into a partnership with the California High-Speed Rail Authority (Authority) to identify and propose corridor-wide, long-term energy resiliency and asset commercialization network (CLEAN) Projects. Under the contemplated Cal CLEAN Partnership, the Authority will initially enter into a Project Identification Agreement (PIA) to serve as an initial agreement under which the Developer will perform due diligence and project identification activities and submit proposals for CLEAN Projects that it wishes to develop within the high-speed rail corridor. 

Pursuant to PUC Section 185036, this procurement includes up to four phases of activities contemplated as part of the Cal CLEAN Partnership, including the ability to enter into three agreements as follows: (1) RFQ Procurement Phase: from the issuance of the RFQ to the execution of the PIA; (2) Project Identification Phase: from execution of the PIA until the end of the PIA term; (3) Pre-Development Procurement Phase; and (4) Development Phase as briefly described below, and more fully described in the RFQ.   

This procurement involves four phases of activities contemplated as part of the Cal CLEAN Partnership as described below.  

Procurement Phase: From the issuance of the RFQ to the execution of the PIA. 

Project Identification Phase: From execution of the PIA until the end of the PIA term (which is currently anticipated to be 6 months). During the Project Identification Phase, the Developers work will include identifying one or more CLEAN Projects for further advancement, including definition of CLEAN Project scope, general technical requirements, high-level costs, and proposal of Pre-Development Phase terms (e.g., regulatory support, cost reimbursement, if any, and property interests such as easements or rights of access needed to advance the proposed CLEAN Project). 

Pre-Development Phase: This phase commences upon the effectiveness of a PDA entered by the Developer and the Authority and ends upon expiry of the term of the PDA (unless terminated earlier). The term of the PDA will be determined by the parties during their collaborative development of the PDA; it is expected to be of a sufficient duration to accommodate the relevant projects regulatory and permitting work, as well as negotiation of a DLA or equivalent governing implementation of the CLEAN Project. 

By the end of the PDA phase, the Developer is expected to provide a binding financial proposal describing the terms for sharing project revenues with the Authority, in addition to the other financial terms of the transaction.  

Development Phase: The period starting from execution of a DLA until the end of the term of such DLA. The term of the DLA will be determined by the parties during their collaborative development of the DLA; it is expected to be a long-term agreement with a sufficient duration to accommodate the relevant CLEAN Project construction, commissioning, and long-term operations and revenue generation. 

The Authority anticipates that the Developer may identify and propose multiple CLEAN Projects during the Project Identification Phase, and that such projects may vary in technology type, site location, development complexity, regulatory pathway, and implementation schedule. Accordingly, the parties may enter into multiple PDAs and DLAs, each governing a discrete CLEAN Project or group of related CLEAN Projects with associated phasing, as well as terms, scope, and duration of each agreement to reflect the specific characteristics and requirements of the applicable CLEAN Project(s). 

The Authority also welcomes additional input on innovative technologies, delivery approaches, or other concepts that may enhance cost efficiency, schedule acceleration, or improve system resilience.  

Procurement Schedule: 
- Release of RFQ: July 9, 2026 
- Virtual Pre-Bid Conference Date: July 15, 2026, 1:00pm PST  
- SOQ Due Date: August 17, 2026 
- Identification of Selected Respondent (Notice of Proposed Award): October 2026 

For more information, please visit: https://hsr.ca.gov/work-with-us/procurements/architectural-engineering-and-capital-contracts/cal-clean-partnership-agreement/ 

Questions regarding this procurement should be submitted to Emily Morrison at CalCLEAN@hsr.ca.gov.

opportunities.title: Water Technical Access Portal (WaterTAP)
opportunities.description:
On behalf of the California State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB), the California Department of Technology seeks proposals from qualified bidders to provide a cloud-based SaaS solution for the Water Technical Access Portal (WaterTAP). These services will include development, design, and implementation of the WaterTAP solution, software licensing and maintenance, and optional post-implementation services.

The WaterTAP solution will replace legacy systems with a configurable, cloud-based Software as a Service (SaaS) solution that will be an enterprise-level data system which aims to minimize customization and:

¿	Address current and future information and business needs, 
¿	Maintain an overarching architecture to connect existing foundational data systems,
¿	Integrate new data systems from disparate spreadsheets to databases currently used, into a single, cohesive system,
¿	Streamline information access for internal staff and external stakeholders,
¿	Supports data and document submissions, workflow routing, and compliance decision support

The WaterTAP cloud-based SaaS solution will enable SWRCB to be more agile in responding to new legislation and to support California's environmental requirements.  It will also create a streamlined user experience, increase efficiency, and create a single system of record for all drinking water reporting. Finally, the WaterTAP cloud-based SaaS solution will also improve access to data for more robust and complete reporting.

opportunities.description:
The California Interagency Council on Homelessness (Cal ICH) serves as a statewide leader, facilitator, and coordinator for policy development and research that supports state, local, and Tribal partners in preventing and ending homelessness in California. Cal ICH is committed to purposeful, action oriented collaboration across member agencies and departments; strong partnerships with local jurisdictions; advancing racial equity and justice; and elevating the expertise of people with lived experience of homelessness.
The Homeless Data Integration System (HDIS) supports Cal ICH¿s mission by collecting and aggregating Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) data from programs across the state into a single, comprehensive reporting platform. HDIS provides an unduplicated count of people accessing homelessness services in California and enables the State to analyze service utilization patterns and understand the characteristics of individuals experiencing homelessness.
HDIS currently receives data from forty four (44) regionally based Continuums of Care (CoCs), each responsible for coordinating housing and services for people experiencing homelessness within defined geographic areas. These CoCs, made up of service providers such as nonprofit organizations and local government entities, implement and manage their own HMIS systems. Each CoC collects data in accordance with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) HMIS Data Standards Manual. While the CoCs provide similar types of data, each operates independently and according to its own local processes.

opportunities.title: Cannabis Integration System (CSI) - DCC
opportunities.description:
The Department of Cannabis Control (DCC) leverages two separate instances of the Accela platform to manage essential business processes related to cannabis licensure, compliance, and enforcement. The two systems, known as the Cannabis Licensing, Enforcement, and Reporting (CLEaR) system and the Cultivation Licensing System (CLS), address distinct aspects of cannabis regulation in California.
The CLEaR system focuses on the licensure and regulatory oversight of cannabis retailers, distributors, laboratories, transporters, microbusinesses, event organizers and manufactured cannabis. The CLS is specifically tailored to support the licensure and oversight of cannabis cultivation activities. Both systems have functionality for monitoring compliance and conducting enforcement activities, ensuring that cultivators adhere to state regulations and maintain high standards for safety, sustainability, and legal operations.
This proposal seeks to consolidate the two Accela systems into one unified system for all Cannabis activities. A centralized database would improve the Department's cannabis oversight by increasing operational efficiency, enhancing data-driven decision-making, streamlining customer service, and accelerating regulatory compliance.
